title: Different Types of Tiles Explained: Clay, Ceramic, Stone and Cement
excerpt: The main tile types for Pakistani homes, clay, ceramic, stone and cement, and which room each one suits.
meta_title: Different Types of Tiles: Clay, Ceramic, Stone, Cement
meta_description: Compare the main types of tiles for Pakistani homes, clay, ceramic, stone and cement, and see which suits each room before you order a sample.
answer_box: The main types of tiles for houses are clay (terracotta, Multani, khaprail), ceramic and porcelain, natural stone and cement or concrete. They differ in porosity, hardness, upkeep and look, so choose by room, water exposure and whether the spot is indoors or outdoors.
ai_summary: Home tiles fall into four families: clay and terracotta, ceramic and porcelain, natural stone, and cement or concrete. Glazed tiles suit wet rooms, clay and cement suit floors and outdoor areas with sealing, and stone suits walls and feature areas. Pak Clay, making clay tiles in Lahore since 1982, offers free samples on WhatsApp.

faqs.question: What are the different types of tiles for a house?
faqs.answer: The main families are clay or terracotta, ceramic and porcelain, natural stone such as granite and marble, and cement or concrete. Each has different water absorption, hardness and upkeep, so match the material to the room.

faqs.question: What is the difference between ceramic and terracotta tiles?
faqs.answer: Ceramic tiles are usually glazed, which makes them easy to wipe and suited to wet rooms. Terracotta is unglazed fired clay with a warm look and a porous surface that benefits from a sealer. Ask each maker for specifications.

faqs.question: How much do different tiles cost?
faqs.answer: Rates depend on material, size, finish, quantity, delivery and the date of the quote, so no fixed figure applies. Ask for a dated written quote in one unit, such as per square foot, and compare like with like.

faqs.question: Which tile is best for a Pakistani summer?
faqs.answer: Many people choose clay or light-coloured stone for floors and shaded outdoor areas because they feel comfortable underfoot, but surface temperature also depends on sun exposure and colour. Check a sample in your own space.

faqs.question: How do I choose the right tile for my room?
faqs.answer: List the room, water exposure, grip needs and whether it is indoors or outdoors. Then ask for a sample, view it in daylight, and send your area and city to Pak Clay on WhatsApp for a free sample and a dated quote.
